knowledge:
- key_parameters: cl.cores=An option list parameter to set the number of cores for multiprocessing ;; msaPath=The file path to the multiple sequence alignment file in addMSA ;; msaFormat=The format of the alignment file (e.g., "fasta") in addMSA ;; makePlot=A logical parameter in sneakPeek to generate a threshold preassessment plot ;; threshold=The second argument in lineagePath representing the major SNP threshold used to resolve lineages ;; minSNP=The minimum number of SNPs required for parallel mutation detection in parallelSites ;; mutMode=The mode for defining parallel mutations in parallelSites (options: "all", "exact", "pre", "post")
- alternatives: ape=CRAN package providing basic parsing functions for reading tree files ;; treeio=Bioconductor package providing more comprehensive phylogenetic tree parsing utilities ;; seqinr=CRAN package for parsing various multiple sequence alignment formats
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have a single phylogenetic tree and a corresponding multiple sequence alignment of viral sequences, and you want to identify fixed substitutions (associated with maintaining viral function) and parallel mutations (reflecting adaptive selection/evolution).
- pitfalls: Using an unrooted tree or a tree with super long branches can lead to poor results; it is highly recommended to use a rooted tree with no super long branches. Setting cl.cores to 1 in options will disable multiprocessing; set it higher to speed up computation. Choosing an inappropriate threshold for lineagePath can affect lineage resolution; use sneakPeek first to sample thresholds and find a stable value.

workflows.name: fixed_and_parallel_mutations_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify fixed substitutions and parallel mutations from a phylogenetic tree and multiple sequence alignment.
input: tree_file (a rooted phylogenetic tree file, e.g., in Newick format)
alignment_file (a multiple sequence alignment file, e.g., in FASTA format)
workflows.stages: 1. Import phylogenetic tree using read.tree ;; 2. Import and align sequence data with the tree using addMSA ;; 3. Pre-assess lineage thresholds using sneakPeek ;; 4. Resolve phylogenetic pathways using lineagePath ;; 5. Perform entropy minimization using sitesMinEntropy ;; 6. Detect fixation sites using fixationSites ;; 7. Detect parallel mutation sites using parallelSites ;; 8. Extract and visualize specific sites using extractSite, extractTips, plotSingleSite, and plot
workflows.code:
library(sitePath)

tree_file <- system.file("extdata", "ZIKV.newick", package = "sitePath")
tree <- read.tree(tree_file)

alignment_file <- system.file("extdata", "ZIKV.fasta", package = "sitePath")

options(list("cl.cores" = 1)) # Set this bigger than 1 to use multiprocessing

paths <- addMSA(tree, msaPath = alignment_file, msaFormat = "fasta")

preassessment <- sneakPeek(paths, makePlot = TRUE)

paths <- lineagePath(preassessment, 18)
paths

plot(paths)

minEntropy <- sitesMinEntropy(paths)

fixations <- fixationSites(minEntropy)
fixations

allSites <- allSitesName(fixations)
allSites

sp <- extractSite(fixations, 139)

extractTips(fixations, 139)

plot(sp)
plotSingleSite(fixations, 139)

plot(fixations)

paraSites <- parallelSites(minEntropy, minSNP = 1, mutMode = "exact")
paraSites

plotSingleSite(paraSites, 105)

plot(paraSites)

plotSingleSite(paths, 139)
plotSingleSite(paths, 763)

snps <- SNPsites(paths)
plotMutSites(snps)
plotSingleSite(paths, snps[4])
plotSingleSite(paths, snps[5])
